population_banner:
POPULATION: this projection covers 48 declared ET-CC members and 29
declared in-population OC checks. That is the slice adjudicated so far,
and it is NOT the whole conformance picture: the full comparison is 281
ET-CC members and 173 in-denominator OC checks, of which 233 members and
130 checks are not_yet_adjudicated -- a third state, distinct from
bucket 1 -- owned by the tickets the crosswalk's own
`outside_the_population` block names. A further 14 checks carry an edge
without being declared by any file, so they are counted in neither.

A count of zero in this view means zero WITHIN THAT SLICE. It does not
mean zero in the suite. As the declared population grows this projection
re-runs and fills.

EVERY FIGURE ABOVE IS INTERPOLATED from the crosswalk being projected;
none is written here. The [population_statement] guard refuses a
population figure that is not.
predicate: Declared-population ET-CC members carrying NO edge in `cells`: the complement of `members_with_edges` over the declared population, taken through `Crosswalk.project(:bucket_1, ...)`. Universe: the 48 declared members, never all 281 members.

rows.the_search_that_found_none: Both CG7 scenarios' fixtures were read at the pinned build. `http-custom-headers` serves two tools and ONE argument vector — the 16 values of the alpha.11 `http-custom-headers` fixture's own argument vector, enumerated in header_mirror_test.exs:305-322 — and no value in it is sentinel-shaped (`=?base64?…?=`); `http-invalid-tool-headers` sends no annotated VALUES at all, only ten malformed tool DEFINITIONS (`Ua`). The 29 CG7 check names were then read for one whose predicate is about a plain value that looks encoded: none is. `Ka` would in fact mis-handle such a value — `Ga` calls it safe, so `Wa` decodes it and the comparison is made against the DECODED form — but no fixture case reaches that path.
rows.why_no_counterpart: streamable-http.mdx:508-510 requires a client to Base64-encode a plain-ASCII value that matches the sentinel pattern, or a server cannot tell an encoded value from a literal one. The scenario exists and is matched; its fixture holds no case that exercises the constraint — which is what `no-oc-fixture-case` names, as against `no-oc-scenario`.

rows.the_search_that_found_none: Every annotated property in both `http-custom-headers` tool schemas is TOP-LEVEL — read at the pinned build: `region`, `priority`, `verbose`, `debug`, `empty_val`, `method_val`, `non_ascii_val`, `whitespace_val`, `leading_space_val`, `trailing_space_val`, `internal_space_val`, `control_char_val`, `crlf_val`, `tab_val`. No fixture tool nests an annotation, so no fixture call can distinguish reading the annotated PATH from reading a same-named key anywhere. The 29 check names were read for one about path resolution: none is.
rows.why_no_counterpart: Distinct from `CG7-static-reachability`, which is about whether a nested annotation is VALID. This is about which value is read at call time once it is. Both are unexercised by the fixture, for the same reason and by two different constraints.

member.test: test value encoding — the fixture's own 16-value vector no header carries a raw CR or LF — injection is closed by construction

rows.the_search_that_found_none: All 29 CG7 checks were read. Each `ClientCustomHeader_*` check's predicate quantifies over ONE named header — `checkParamHeader` is called once per annotated parameter and `a=e.headers[i]` reads that parameter's header alone. No check's predicate quantifies over the header SET, and neither `ClientSupportsCustomHeaders` (`some(...)`, an existential over names, not values) nor the two NoMirror checks (`===void 0` on one named header) is universal either.
rows.why_no_counterpart: The member asserts a UNIVERSAL property — no produced header value carries a raw CR or LF, and every produced header NAME is lower-case — over the whole 16-value vector. It is the injection-closure property, and it is stronger than the conjunction of the per-parameter checks: it would still fail if a SEVENTEENTH header appeared carrying a newline. Filing it on `ClientCustomHeader_CrLf` would report agreement on a check whose subject is one header's value.

rows.the_search_that_found_none: The scenario's client driver always issues tools/list before tools/call — indeed `http-invalid-tool-headers` emits a FAILING gate check when it does not (`sep-2243-invalid-tool-tools-list-gate`, which A5 leaves in the denominator). So no fixture case reaches a tools/call with no prior listing. All 29 CG7 check names were read for one whose subject is mirroring in the ABSENCE of a schema: none is.
rows.why_no_counterpart: The member's remaining claim — that the `mcp-name` routing header still rides the call — does have a counterpart, `ClientMcpNameHeader_tools_call`, but it is CG1's and outside this file's declared check population. So this member has no counterpart HERE, which is what `declared_unmatched` means in a file that declares its own check population; the CG1 claim is recorded under `claims_without_an_edge` and routed to C1b-ii.
